question: Should OpenClaw expose a shared, bounded operator configuration for exec-approval lifetime, and if so should it be scoped only to exec approvals or to the generic approval subsystem?
rationale: This adds public configuration governing a host-exec authorization window; source-level plumbing cannot determine the intended security scope, permanent key placement, or acceptable range.

options.title: Adopt one exec-scoped setting
options.body: Add one schema-validated exec approval timeout with a conservative cap, unchanged default, shared TTL/RPC derivation, documentation, and focused security tests.

options.title: Design a generic approvals contract
options.body: First define a shared approval-timeout API if product intent is to govern more than exec approvals, then migrate exec to that contract.

options.title: Keep the fixed policy
options.body: Decline a public timeout override and instead improve notification or approval-surface reliability for missed requests.

recommendation.title: Adopt one exec-scoped setting
recommendation.body: Add one schema-validated exec approval timeout with a conservative cap, unchanged default, shared TTL/RPC derivation, documentation, and focused security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent proposal explicitly identifies the key-placement choice, security cap, and single-source-of-truth behavior that need product calibration.
